cases.description: Calling setTSIG(TSIG) with a non‑null TSIG key should attach a TSIGRecord to the message, set the internal state to TSIG_SIGNED and make isSigned() return true.

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() == false && Message.getTSIG() == null && Message.tsigState == Message.TSIG_UNSIGNED
cases.description: Passing null to setTSIG(TSIG) should clear any existing TSIG, reset the state to TSIG_UNSIGNED and ensure the message is not considered signed.
When the three‑argument overload is invoked with an error code other than NOERROR, the method should mark the TSIG processing as failed (TSIG_FAILED) and the message must not be considered signed.
First call attaches an initial TSIG.
Calling setTSIG again with a different key should replace the existing TSIGRecord and keep the state as TSIG_SIGNED.
When a query TSIGRecord is supplied and the MAC verification succeeds, the method should set the state to TSIG_VERIFIED and isVerified() must return true.

input.value: new TSIGRecord(Name.fromString("example.com."), DClass.IN, 300, new TSIG("hmac-md5", "wrong".getBytes()), new byte[0])

cases.description: If the supplied query TSIGRecord does not match the key (MAC verification fails), the method must transition to TSIG_FAILED and verification flag stays false.
If the method is called during message construction (no query TSIG and no error), it should place the TSIG in an intermediate state awaiting final signing.

group: Idempotent setTSIG on already signed message

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() == true && Message.getTSIG() != null && Message.tsigState == Message.TSIG_SIGNED && Message.getTSIG().getAlgorithm().equals("hmac-sha256")
cases.description: First call attaches a TSIG and marks the message as signed. A second call with the same TSIG instance should leave the message in the same TSIG_SIGNED state without creating a second TSIGRecord.

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() == true && Message.getTSIG() != null && Message.tsigState == Message.TSIG_SIGNED && Message.getTSIG().getAlgorithm().equals("hmac-sha256")
cases.description: Calling setTSIG(TSIG) twice consecutively with an identical key must be a no‑op after the first successful attachment; the internal state and TSIGRecord remain unchanged.

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() == true && Message.getTSIG() != null && Message.getTSIG().getKey().length == 0 && Message.tsigState == Message.TSIG_SIGNED
cases.description: A TSIG whose secret is an empty byte array is still a valid key for the library; setTSIG should attach it and mark the message as signed.
If the algorithm string is not one of the algorithms supported by the TSIG implementation, setTSIG(TSIG) must throw an IllegalArgumentException.

group: Set TSIG after successful verification resets verification flag

input.value: new TSIGRecord(Name.fromString("example.com."), DClass.IN, 300, new TSIG("hmac-md5", "secret".getBytes()), new byte[0])

cases.description: First, use the three‑argument overload to simulate a verified incoming TSIG (state = TSIG_VERIFIED).

cases.expected: Message.isSigned() == true && Message.isVerified() == false && Message.tsigState == Message.TSIG_SIGNED
cases.description: Calling the one‑argument setTSIG(TSIG) after a verified state must replace the TSIGRecord and reset the verification flag, leaving the message in the normal signed state.

group: Replace TSIG with same algorithm but different secret

cases.description: Attach an initial TSIG using algorithm hmac‑sha1 and secret "first".
Calling setTSIG again with the same algorithm but a different secret must replace the existing TSIGRecord while keeping the message signed.

group: Set TSIG after intermediate state transition

cases.description: Use the three‑argument overload to place the message in the intermediate state (no query TSIG, no error).
Calling the one‑argument setTSIG(TSIG) after an intermediate state should finalize the TSIG, moving the state to TSIG_SIGNED and marking the message as signed.
Creating a TSIG with a null algorithm string should cause the TSIG constructor (and thus setTSIG) to throw IllegalArgumentException.
Creating a TSIG with a null secret byte array must raise IllegalArgumentException because the secret cannot be null.

group: Invalid error code in three‑argument overload

cases.description: Passing an error code outside the valid Rcode range to setTSIG(TSIG, int, TSIGRecord) should result in IllegalArgumentException.

group: TSIG attached to another Message (illegal state)

cases.description: If a TSIG instance has already been associated with a different Message (simulated by calling setTSIG on a first Message and then on a second Message without cloning), the second call should throw IllegalStateException because a TSIG cannot be reused across messages.
